content:
emma: rolling back the recent device lockdown in the base image — staging jobs started failing after the build at 07:32 UTC, multiple test runners hit pty errors.

sam: saw the same. failures show `open /dev/ptmx: permission denied` and some containers can't spawn shells. reproducible in local run with the new image.

kai: that change tightened device access to reduce surface area (no /dev/*). didn't expect interactive-based test runners to depend on pty.

maria: @sam @kai oncall here — is rollback the safest path? can we do a targeted RBAC tweak instead?

sam: fastest is rollback to image tag `rbase-2026-03-20a`. downside: the new image introduced KMS-backed attestation signing which will also revert. need to coordinate KMS IAM too.

emma: agreed. if we rollback we must temporarily restore the signing flow or ensure the old image can sign via existing key. propose: short-lived binding for the build SA to `keystore:sign` for 30-60m.

jen: SRE note — enable audit logging for the KMS key before doing any temporary RBAC changes. we need to capture `CryptoKeyVersion` calls and image pull auth. retention at 90d preferred for triage.

sam: minimal IAM snippet that would let the build service sign (example):
```
resource "google_kms_crypto_key_iam_binding" "build_signer" {
  role    = "roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter"
  members = ["serviceAccount:build-service@redwood-inference.iam.gserviceaccount.com"]
}
```

kai: prefer scoping to a signer role but cloud provider constraints mean we may need encrypter/decrypter. also: don't bind the long-lived build-service SA — use short-lived SA impersonation via `sts:impersonate`.

emma: decision: rollback image now, create a short-lived service account for attestation signing, apply timebound IAM binding (1h), enable audit logs, then run canary. I'll coordinate release.

maria: created INC-2026-03-3999, enabling debug audit logs for KMS and image registry, and started collecting affected container IDs. link: https://internal-redwood/incident/INC-2026-03-3999

jen: follow-up action: add CI gate test that checks `/dev/ptmx` is accessible for runner images, e.g. `docker run --rm image /bin/sh -c "test -e /dev/ptmx && echo ok"`. add to PR checks for base-image changes.

sam: performing rollback now. deploy-bot kicking off staged rollout to staging.

deploy-bot: rollout -> starting: image=rbase-2026-03-20a, scope=staging

deploy-bot: rollout 10% -> success

deploy-bot: rollout 100% -> success :white_check_mark:

kai: canary green. I'll prepare a follow-up patch that grants only `/dev/ptmx` access via group membership rather than broad device allowances. that should preserve attack-surface reduction intent.

emma: also update pod security settings: PSP/PodSecurityPolicy equivalent needs an explicit `devices: ["/dev/ptmx"]` exception for the CI namespace. assign to kai + jen.

sam: assigned to @kai and @jen. I'll apply the short-lived KMS binding and then revoke. will post the IAM diff in the ticket.

maria: keeping incident open for postmortem scheduling. will collect logs and timeline. closing this chat thread, thanks all :thumbsup:
